candidates.attacker_control: The `counter` request parameter of the monitoring URL (`?action=clear_counter&counter=<payload>`) is fully attacker-controlled and is echoed into the inline JavaScript unencoded. Example payload (safe description): `x';alert(document.domain);//` percent-encoded. The sibling `part` parameter is likewise unencoded at HtmlCoreReport.java:316 and reaches the same sink on the collector-server deployment through `CollectorController.writeMessage` (lines 407-411), which passes the request `part` to `writeMessageIfNotNull`.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that (a) the adjacent `message` string is `javascriptEncode`d while the anchor is not, so this is not general encoding inside the helper; (b) `writeDirectly` performs no encoding and `I18N.writeTo` only replaces `#key#` translations; (c) `getContextName` has no validation path; (d) `Collector.getCounterByName` returning null does not abort the action (no exception, message still non-null); (e) CLEAR_COUNTER is explicitly exempt from the system-actions check; (f) the monitoring URI check in MonitoringFilter is satisfied by the plain monitoring URL and `part` can be omitted; (g) other report sinks generally use `htmlEncode`/`javascriptEncode`/`urlEncode`, which makes this omission look like a genuine defect rather than a deliberate convention.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary JavaScript executes in the origin of the JavaMelody monitoring report with the victim's session and privileges: session/CSRF-token theft (where cookies are not HttpOnly), reading of exposed monitoring data (HTTP sessions and session attributes, database/JNDI/MBean information), and performing monitoring actions as the victim (GC, heap dump, thread kill, session invalidation, cache purge, collector add/remove application). In the Jira/Bamboo/Confluence plugin filter deployments the victim is a system administrator, so the XSS operates with system-admin authority.
candidates.prerequisites: A victim with access to the monitoring report must open the crafted URL (reflected XSS); typically the monitoring page is an admin/ops page protected by container security constraints or `javamelody.allowed-addr-pattern`, so this is a link/phishing or allowed-network attack. No `javamelody.system-actions-enabled` setting is required because CLEAR_COUNTER skips `checkSystemActionsEnabled`, and the request must not include a `part` parameter (that would route away from `toHtml(message, anchor)`). On the collector server the `part` variant additionally requires at least one monitored application so `writeMessage` uses the report path instead of `showAlertAndRedirectTo`.
candidates.root_cause: `HtmlCoreReport.writeMessageIfNotNull` (javamelody-core/src/main/java/net/bull/javamelody/HtmlCoreReport.java:296-320) builds a `<script>` block: `alert("…");` (message is escaped via `javascriptEncode`) followed by `location.href = location.href.substring(0, location.href.indexOf('?')) + '#<anchorNameForRedirect>';` / `location.href = '#<anchorNameForRedirect>';` (lines 309-312) and `location.href = '?part=<partToRedirectTo>'` (line 316). The anchor and part values are written with `writeDirectly` and never encoded. For `action=clear_counter`, `MonitoringController.executeActionIfNeeded` (MonitoringController.java:102-120) sets `anchorNameForRedirect = Action.getContextName(counterName)`, and `Action.getContextName` (Action.java:127-132) returns the raw request parameter `counter` whenever it is not "all". `MonitoringController` only enforces `checkSystemActionsEnabled()` for actions other than CLEAR_COUNTER (line 109), and `Collector.clearCounter` (Collector.java:876-889) silently no-ops for unknown counter names, so no validation rejects the payload. A `'` in `counter` terminates the JS string literal and allows arbitrary script to run.
candidates.title: Reflected XSS in monitoring report: unencoded `counter` parameter injected into inline JavaScript in HtmlCoreReport.writeMessageIfNotNull
candidates.trace: GET <context>/monitoring?action=clear_counter&counter=x%27;alert(document.domain);// -> MonitoringFilter.doFilter (MonitoringFilter.java:171-173, exact monitoring URI) -> doMonitoring -> MonitoringController.doActionIfNeededAndReport (line 342) -> executeActionIfNeeded: `counter` read at line 112, `Action.CLEAR_COUNTER.execute` -> `clearCounter` returns a non-null message, `anchorNameForRedirect = action.getContextName(counterName)` returns the raw parameter (lines 117-119) -> doReport/doReportCore -> doCompressedHtml -> HtmlController.doHtml: `part == null` so `htmlReport.toHtml(messageForReport, anchorNameForRedirect)` (HtmlController.java:98-99) -> HtmlReport.toHtml -> HtmlCoreReport.toHtml -> writeMessageIfNotNull -> raw `writeDirectly("location.href = … + '#" + anchorNameForRedirect + "';")`.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and no HTTP request was sent; the runtime response/script execution was not observed. Deployment-specific access control on /monitoring and browser behavior were not exercised. The exact upstream fix commit for this code is unknown; identification with a specific historic advisory/CVE is not claimed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

coverage_summary: Reviewed the core web/monitoring path in depth: MonitoringFilter/PluginMonitoringFilter/JiraMonitoringFilter, MonitoringController, Action, HtmlController, HtmlReport, HtmlCoreReport and the HTML report classes (session, counter, thread, process, MBeans, JNDI, database, heap histogram), Collector/CollectorController/CollectorServlet/CollectorServer, RemoteCollector, LabradorRetriever, TransportFormat, CounterStorage, SessionListener/SessionInformations, DatabaseInformations, JndiBinding, MBeans, Parameters/Parameter/HttpParameters, I18N/LOG. The P1 relation index covers 291/343 visible Java files (syntax-only: containment, name/type/arity call and inheritance candidates, 962 facts; no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, or Spring runtime enforcement), so annotations, runtime wiring and full call/data flow were not inferred from it. Not reviewed in depth: javamelody-swing module, iText/PDF rendering internals, JRobin internals, JavaScript resources, JdbcWrapper/JdbcWrapperHelper internals, build files.
limitations: No code execution, tests, or HTTP requests were performed; all conclusions are static source evidence only.
The P1 index is partial and syntax-based with no data-flow/control-flow/reachability proofs; every edge used was re-checked against source text.

Deployment-specific access controls for /monitoring (container security constraints, allowed-addr-pattern, Jira/Confluence plugin auth) were not resolvable from the snapshot and affect exploitability.
The exact upstream fix commit/version and any CVE correspondence for this code could not be checked offline; the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed or runtime-verified vulnerability.
Files excluded by scope filters: 1 sensitive-name/path file; binaries would be skipped but none appeared in the source tree.

rejected_leads.lead: Stored XSS via the `X-Forwarded-For` request header: MonitoringFilter.java:313-323 stores `remoteAddr + \" forwarded for \" + forwardedFor` in the session, and HtmlSessionInformationsReport.java:315-325 writes `remoteAddr` unencoded into the sessions table.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible second root cause but weaker: the header is only captured when the session is first created, and viewing requires the `part=sessions` page (gated by `checkSystemActionsEnabled`) plus an admin victim. Kept as an unconfirmed lead, not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: `part` parameter injected unencoded at HtmlCoreReport.java:316 in the collector-server path (CollectorController.writeMessage lines 407-411).
rejected_leads.reason: Same unescaped JavaScript block, but requires the separate collector-server deployment and a non-null message (action or exception); treated as part of the same root cause rather than a separate candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: `CollectorController.showAlertAndRedirectTo` (lines 433-443) writes `redirectTo` raw into `location.href`; CollectorServlet.doPost (lines 138-140) passes `"?application=" + appName` from a POST parameter.
rejected_leads.reason: Potential XSS on the collector server, but it needs a POST to the collector servlet with a valid app URL and was not traced to a rendered response as firmly; unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: `DatabaseInformations.explainPlanFor` (lines 329-370) runs `statement.execute(\"explain plan … for <sql>\")` on SQL taken from the `request` HTTP header via SerializableController (lines 188-191), without a system-actions check.
rejected_leads.reason: Oracle-only and `EXPLAIN PLAN FOR` plans rather than executes DML; concrete data/command impact could not be established from source, so not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: `collector=stop` (MonitoringFilter.java:345-361) clears counters and stops collection with no authorization check.
rejected_leads.reason: State-changing but only reachable by a client already able to reach the monitoring URL; design-level issue, lower impact than the XSS.

rejected_leads.lead: Collector server accepts application URLs and later Java-deserializes HTTP responses (LabradorRetriever.java:279-302).
rejected_leads.reason: Inherent collector design reachable only by users able to add applications; no authentication analysis was possible and impact depends on deployment; not submitted.

summary: JavaMelody 1.47.0-SNAPSHOT monitoring webapp. The HTML report emits an inline JavaScript alert/redirect block in `HtmlCoreReport.writeMessageIfNotNull`. The alert `message` is passed through `javascriptEncode`, but `anchorNameForRedirect` (lines 309-312) and `partToRedirectTo` (line 316) are concatenated raw into single-quoted JS strings via `writeDirectly`. For `action=clear_counter`, `anchorNameForRedirect` is set directly from the request's `counter` parameter (`Action.getContextName` returns it verbatim when it is not "all"), and `Collector.clearCounter` tolerates unknown counter names, so no validation blocks a payload. A crafted monitoring URL therefore yields reflected cross-site scripting in the monitoring/admin origin. I submit this single candidate; other plausible but weaker/unconfirmed leads are listed separately.
